idiom_name: TCA @Reducer: State + Action + Reduce { state, action in ... } + Store.send
implementation_notes: Swift's most established realization is The Composable Architecture: a feature declares State (an @ObservableState value type), Action (an enum covering user actions and effect results), a reducer body built with Reduce { state, action in ... } that mutates state and returns Effects, and views drive a StoreOf<Feature> by sending actions while the store runs reducers/effects and republishes state. TCA supplies the runtime parts MVI leaves to the framework (effect scheduling, feature composition, test tools), which is why Swift is classified as library; for simple screens SwiftUI's own Observation framework gives the lighter state-holder route, and that hand-rolled variant is recorded below.
pitfalls: Reducers run on the main actor: blocking work inside reduce freezes the UI; return .run effects for I/O and await inside them.
State is a value type, but nested reference types inside it still mutate shared snapshots; keep the state tree value-typed.
State read outside the view body (or in a plain property) is not observed; read State properties inside the body or use @ObservableState bindings.
Effects capturing self or the store strongly keep features alive after dismissal; capture deliberately and cancel long-running effects on teardown.

variants.name: Hand-rolled MVI: @Observable state holder + intent enum + reduce + AsyncStream effects
variants.idiom_name: @Observable final class holder + enum Intent + reduce(state, intent) + AsyncStream effects
variants.implementation_notes: The framework-only route: an @Observable class (Observation, Swift 5.9+) owns the immutable State value, user actions are an Intent enum funnelled through send(_:), a pure reduce(state, intent) computes the next state, and one-shot work runs as Tasks whose results are sent back as intents (or through an AsyncStream of effects). Views read the state properties they render, so observation re-renders them; choose this when no third-party architecture is wanted and the feature is small, and prefer TCA once composition, effect management and integration tests matter.
pitfalls: Mutating the holder off the main actor interleaves UI updates; mark it @MainActor or marshal sends to the main thread.
Observation tracks only properties read during body evaluation; derived values computed outside the body do not trigger updates.
Holding the model in @State per view creates one model per screen; app-wide state needs the single instance at the App/Scene level.
Effects started in send() must be cancelled when the screen disappears, or stale results are sent back into a dead state holder.
